title: SDK empathy maps and sample UX flows — sprint notes
content:
Context:
This doc captures a sprint's worth of notes exploring 'empathy-driven' SDK quickstarts: map common adopter mindsets, define very small UX flows that match them, and produce a short checklist + experiments list we can ship as a companion to the starter SDK.

Problem statement:
- Many first-time SDK users bail at network/credential errors or when they hit a usage-cost surprise.
- Current quickstarts are feature-centric (auth, call, parse) but don’t surface likely failure states tied to user intent.
- We want a tiny set of UX flows that map to adopter intents so support/telemetry + docs can preempt confusion.

Goals for this sprint:
1) Produce 4 empathy maps for distinct adopter types.
2) Sketch 3 single-file quickstart flows that are <10 lines for each language (py/js) showing best-practice error handling and telemetry hooks.
3) Create a mini-checklist (5 items) teams can adopt into their repo templates.
4) Define 5 lightweight experiments to validate the flows with real internal users.

Adopter Personas (high level):
- Prototype PM (wants rapid demo): cares about speed-to-demo, uses sample inputs, hates long config.
- Infra Engineer (wants reliability): cares about retries, timeouts, idempotency, cost controls.
- Data-hungry Researcher (wants fidelity): cares about model versioning, deterministic outputs, eval hooks.
- Nonengineer Integrator (designer/customer-success): needs copy examples, canned responses, minimal code.

Empathy map template (used for each persona):
- Says: short quotes we might see in Slack/email
- Thinks: underlying concerns (cost, speed, security)
- Does: actions they take (runs sample app, pastes tokens, opens ticket)
- Feels: emotional state at first failure (confused, nervous)
- Failure states to preempt: quick bullet list we turn into UX copy or telemetry triggers

Example empathy map (Prototype PM):
- Says: "I just need something to show in the 10am demo."
- Thinks: "If I can get a 1-min demo, I can sell the idea."
- Does: Copies example code, runs locally, pastes API key into env, uses default sample prompt.
- Feels: Frustrated when errors or long cold-starts happen.
- Failure states: Missing API key, rate-limit 429 on rapid click, slow response >2s for sample.

Quickstart UX flows (high-level sketches):
- Flow A: "Zero-friction demo" (Prototype PM)
  - 1) copy starter repo, 2) set REDWOOD_API_KEY in shell, 3) run python demo.py, 4) click `generate` -> successful sample text.
  - UX features: inline env-checks that print clear next-step (e.g., \"no API key detected: run 'export REDWOOD_API_KEY=...'\"), builtin minimal spinner with estimated ETA, fallback to a tiny cached sample if first request times out.

- Flow B: "Safe-by-default" (Infra Engineer)
  - 1) sample shows safe defaults: 3s timeout, exponential backoff, token-limit cap. 2) telemetry hook registers request id, model version and cost estimate. 3) if request is hitting quota limit, SDK surfaces a clear error with suggested mitigation (reduce max_tokens or switch model).

- Flow C: "Deterministic research harness" (Researcher)
  - 1) explicit model pin in example (model: 'redwood-alpha-v1@2024-02-01'), 2) seed control knob exposed, 3) optional write-to-disk of raw responses for eval.

- Flow D: "Copy-first embedder" (Nonengineer Integrator)
  - 1) one-click script that bundles auth via instructions, displays canned prompt library, and shows curated outputs and copy suggestions.

Concise sample code (proto pseudocode included in docs):
- Python (zero-friction):
  - # check env, friendly message if missing
  - # small wrapper that retries once then shows cached sample
  - (we'll keep exact snippets in GH PR 482)

Checklist (repo template):
- 1) Readme: 3-sentence value prop + one-liner run command.
- 2) Perf: set default timeout=3000ms, set max_tokens=256 in examples.
- 3) Safe defaults: enable retries=2, enable simple rate-limit guidance text.
- 4) Telemetry: emit request_id and model_version in logs for every SDK call.
- 5) Troubleshooting: include a troubleshooting.md with the 7 most common errors and recovery steps.

Experiments backlog (short descriptions):
- EXP-1: Ship the zero-friction Python flow to 10 internal PMs; collect success time-to-first-result. (Owner: Maya)
- EXP-2: Add a telemetry event for 'missing_api_key' and measure frequency across new signups. (Owner: Liam)
- EXP-3: A/B test the presence of a cached-sample fallback vs. spinner for first-run latency perception. (Owner: Jordan)
- EXP-4: Run a 30-min session with nonengineer integrators and observe where they pause in the quickstart. (Owner: Priya)
- EXP-5: Add a short interactive shell helper (CLI) that validates network+auth before running; measure reduction in support tickets. (Owner: TBD)

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How opinionated should the SDK be about default timeouts and retries? (we want safe defaults but not surprise slowdowns for high-throughput users)
- Do we ship the cached-sample fallback in the published SDK or keep behind a feature flag for hosted customers? (cost/consistency trade-off)
- How to surface cost estimates in a way that is accurate enough but inexpensive to compute? (estimate vs. exact billing)

Known references and threads:
- Slack thread: #devexp quickstart-rewrite (see messages 2024-02-10..2024-02-14)
- GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/482 (starter repo + tests)
- Jira: DEVEXP-321 quickstart telemetry events
- Confluence outline: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DEX/Quickstart+microflows

Next steps (this sprint):
- Finalize 4 empathy maps and add a 1-line hook per failure state to the troubleshooting doc. (due 2024-03-01)
- Draft the short Python quickstart file and add to PR 482 for review. (due 2024-03-06)
- Instrument telemetry events for 'first_run_success' and 'first_run_failure' temporarily for internal traffic. (due 2024-03-08)

Notes to self (scratchpad):
- Keep sample prompts short — avoid hallucination-heavy examples for demos.
- Add a tiny paragraph about model fallbacks: when to prefer lower-cost variants.
- Remind SRE that sample repo should not consume burst credits in shared infra.

Unresolved and TODO (short):
- [ ] Owner for EXP-5 (CLI validation helper).
- [ ] Decide feature flag strategy for cached sample fallback.
- [ ] Get a legal thumbs-up for shipping embedded sample outputs in public starter repo.

End of sprint notes.
